subject: HelixData POC kickstart: scope, success metrics, prompt set & access
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Hayes <oliver@helixdata.com>, Sana Kapoor <sana.kapoor@helixdata.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: HelixData discovery — proposed POC scope and next steps

Hi Oliver / Sana,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciate the clear framing. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we can kick the POC next week if this looks right.

Key pain points you described:
- Customer support agents are spending ~25% of time handling repetitive billing and plan-change questions (high error rate when looking up entitlements).
- Latency and hallucination risk when routing to existing generative assistants; current rule-based heuristics miss context across sessions.
- Need strict audit trails and control over data residency for PII in transcripts.

POC goal (30 days):
- Demonstrate 2x decrease in avg handle time for top 5 billing intents, with no increase in hallucination incidents (measured by our eval suite).
- Show stable median inference latency <= 180ms for 95th percentile within your expected concurrency.

Proposed scope / deliverables:
1) Data & access: sample conversational logs ingestion (anonymized) + service account access for S3 bucket with transcripts.
2) Prompt/eval plan: we will run a 150-case prompt set (you review) and continuous evals each week.
3) Integration: a proof-of-concept agent endpoint behind your staging environment and a small UI to run batched tests.
4) Metrics dashboard: shared Redwood Console view for latency, cost-per-token, and a hallucination/regression alert.

Owners & timeline:
- Ben Carter (Sales / POC lead) — project owner, weekly syncs
- Monica Patel (CS Ops) — evaluation criteria, dashboard config
- Karthik Iyer (Engineering) — infra + access setup
- Helix: Oliver (Product owner), Sana (Security/compliance lead)

Near-term asks (if agreed):
- Please confirm: we can get a staging S3 share + one service account with read-only access by Friday 9/17.
- Share any compliance checklist (SOC2/PCI) items that would block access.
- Quick review of the attached POC charter and the sample schema I referenced.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-poc-charter.pdf (PDF, 480KB)], [Attachment: helix-sample-schema.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

If that aligns, I’ll schedule a 45-minute kickoff for Monday to run through access and owners.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0119
From: Oliver Hayes <oliver@helixdata.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Sana Kapoor <sana.kapoor@helixdata.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 12:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixData discovery — proposed POC scope and next steps

Thanks Ben — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Data residency / compliance: we need the POC environment to sit in our US-east account and maintain audit logs for all query transcripts. We can’t use external managed storage for raw PII-containing logs; instead we can provide an anonymized export and an internal staging S3 bucket. Sana, can you confirm the exact artifacts we need to provide?

2) Latency: the 180ms 95th target is ambitious but fair. Our traffic shape during peak support hours is spiky — 80 concurrent sessions, bursts to ~180. Can Redwood confirm how batching will behave under burst?

3) Prompt set: attaching a short sample of 40 anonymized tickets for your eval. We’ll need to review the final prompt wording before you run any tests.

We can provide the service account by Friday; will need an internal ticket documenting the least-privilege role. 

Oliver
Oliver Hayes
Head of Product, HelixData
oliver@helixdata.com | +1 617-555-0202

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixData discovery — proposed POC scope and next steps

Appreciate the quick notes, Oliver — answers inline below and next steps at the bottom.

1) Data residency / compliance: understood. Our plan is to run model inference in a customer-controlled VPC (Redwood Private) in your US-east account for the POC; raw transcripts remain in your staging S3. We will only store derived metadata (intent labels, eval results) in Redwood Console with retention set per your policy.

2) Batching/latency under burst: Redwood supports continuous batching with strict latency SLOs; for spikes we have automatic backpressure and can route to a higher-priority dedicated pool (short-lived burst capacity). I’ve asked Karthik to confirm the expected instance sizing and we’ll propose a config that meets the 95th percentile target.

3) Prompt set / evals: thanks for the sample. Monica will share a proposed 150-case prompt matrix by Friday for your review; we will not run it until you sign off on wording.

Action items / timeline:
- Fri 2026-09-17: Helix to provide staging S3 access + least-privilege service account (Oliver / Sana).
- Fri 2026-09-17: Redwood to share the 150-case prompt matrix for review (Monica).
- Mon 2026-09-20: 45-minute POC kickoff (owners + engineering) — propose 10:00 AM ET.
- Weeks 1-4: ingest data, iterate prompts, weekly evals, and mid-point sync at Day 14.

I’ll provision a private Redwood Console dashboard and send a HubSpot link for tracking the deal once we have the S3 access. Also linking the SOW/DocuSign placeholder for procurement.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-helix-poc (POC folder)

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Ben

Ben / team — quick engineering note before kickoff:
- I can stand up the Private deployment in Helix's US-east account once we receive the IAM role and S3 read policy.
- For the burst capacity to work we should target g5.2xlarge-equivalent instances (I’ll provide exact CPU/GPU counts in the infra ticket).
- Please ensure the sample CSV does not include unredacted PII; we will reject datasets with direct identifiers.

Forwarded for visibility: 'Oliver, Sana — please see the attached access checklist and the minimal IAM policy we’ll need. We also added a small README for how Redwood will ingest the anonymized exports.'
